&nbsp; 3. 함정 ② 모두의 데이터 — 갓테이블의 유혹: 3. Trap ②: Everyone's data and the temptation of the God Table
경계선을 그었다면 다음 질문이 기다립니다. <b>\"그래서 이 데이터는: Once the boundaries are drawn, the next question awaits: "So whose data is this?" Every monolithic system has a giant table where columns from every domain, sales, marketing, reservations, and more, are tangled together. This is the so-called God Table. Because every domain depends on this one table, a change in one domain spreads to all the others, and the central database becomes a bottleneck. If you leave the God Table in place and split only the application, you end up with the shared database anti-pattern, where every service clings to a single DB and the point of MSA is lost.
<b style=\"font-weight: bold;\">📍 데이터 지역: 📍 Data Locality: each bounded context owns locally only the data it frequently reads and writes within its own problem space. Entities from other domains are referenced only by an ID Value Object, never pulled in wholesale.
<b style=\"font-weight: bold;\">📋 공통 데이터: 📋 Common Data Duplication: data that rarely changes, such as names and gender, is replicated to each service via events. The key is letting go of the monolith-era normalization instinct that "duplication is always evil." Replication is the price of autonomy, and it is far cheaper than the cost of synchronization.
<b style=\"font-weight: bold;\">📞 원격 호출은: 📞 Remote Invocation as a Last Resort: only data that changes too often to replicate is fetched at call time, and caching and the flyweight pattern reduce call cost and vulnerability to failures.
이 세 원칙의 우선순위가 중요합니다. <b>지역화 먼저, 그다음 복제,: The priority among these three principles matters. Localize first, then replicate, and use remote calls last. Many projects apply this order in reverse (solving everything with remote calls) and slide right back into the chatty microservice of trap ①.

&nbsp; 4. 함정 ③ 사라진 트랜잭션 — 일관성과 성능의 줄다리기: 4. Trap ③: The vanished transaction and the tug-of-war between consistency and performance
모놀리스에서는 당연했던 것이 MSA에서는 사라집니다. 바로 <b>하나의: Something that was taken for granted in a monolith disappears in MSA: the ability to wrap everything in a single transaction. The days of committing the order save and the stock deduction in one transaction are over. The moment data is distributed across services, the safety net of "all succeed or all roll back" is no longer free. This is the most fundamental fear many architects feel when facing MSA.
해답은 <b>일관성의 범위를 재정의</b>하는 데 있습니다. 도메인 주도: The answer lies in redefining the scope of consistency. In Domain-Driven Design (DDD), an Aggregate is "a cluster of objects that must be consistent together, immediately," and it defines the smallest boundary that requires strong consistency. Inside an aggregate, updates are atomic so invariants hold; between aggregates and between services, you manage with eventual consistency — "not necessarily right now, but consistent in the end." The order service saves the order and publishes an event; the inventory service subscribes to it and updates stock at its own pace.
물론 공짜는 아닙니다. 이 스타일을 채택하는 순간 따라오는 숙제들이 있습: It isn't free, of course. The moment you adopt this style, a set of homework comes with it.

모든 서비스가 한 DB를 공유, 스키마 변경 공포, 중앙 DB 병목: Every service shares one DB; fear of schema changes; central DB bottleneck
데이터 지역성 → 공통 데이터 복제 → 원격 호출(최후의 수단): Data locality → replication of shared data → remote calls (last resort)
분산 트랜잭션 시도, 2PC의 늪, 정합성 버그와 성능 저하의 악순환: Attempts at distributed transactions, the 2PC swamp, a vicious cycle of consistency bugs and degraded performance

The real reason microservice design is hard is that this sentence is not a technology problem but a question of how deeply you understand the domain. &nbsp; 6. 해답의 청구서 — 라이프사이클 전 단계에서 만나는 난제: 6. The Bill for the Answer — Challenges Across Every Stage of the Lifecycle
여기까지 읽고 \"행위 중심으로 경계를 긋고 이벤트로 연결하면 되는구나\: If you've read this far and concluded, "So I just draw boundaries around behavior and connect them with events," you're only half right. Event-driven microservice architecture (EDMSA) is an outstanding answer for scalability, decoupling, and real-time processing, but the moment you accept this remedy the difficulty doesn't disappear — it changes shape and scatters across every stage of the project lifecycle. As "the complexity of distributed environments" combines with "asynchronous messaging," each stage — design, implementation, operations, deployment — has its own hard problems waiting. Map them out in advance and they become a checklist instead of something to fear.
<b>이벤트의 굵기:</b> 과도하게 세분화하면 메시지 폭증, 너무 크게: Event granularity: Too fine-grained and messages explode; too coarse and coupling rises — finding the right level is the design itself
<b>이벤트 스키마 버전 관리:</b> 하위 호환을 지키며 진화시키는 거: Event schema versioning: Without governance that evolves schemas while preserving backward compatibility (Schema Registry, Avro/Protobuf), consuming services break
<b>2PC의 불가:</b> 단일 ACID 트랜잭션 없이 최종 일관성의: No 2PC: Without a single ACID transaction, the time lag of eventual consistency must be reflected in UX and business logic (settlement updated some time after "order complete")
<b>Saga 설계 복잡성:</b> 실패 시 보상 트랜잭션을 일일이 설계: Saga design complexity: Compensating transactions must be designed one by one for every failure case, and you must also choose between orchestration and choreography
<b>Dual Write 문제:</b> DB 저장은 성공했는데 브로커 발: The dual-write problem: An atomicity crack where the DB write succeeds but the broker publish fails — it must be solved with a Transactional Outbox or CDC (Debezium), adding corresponding infrastructure and development effort
<b>멱등성:</b> At-Least-Once 전달 특성상 중복 수신은: Idempotency: With at-least-once delivery, duplicate receipt is the default — every consumer must be safe against duplicate execution
<b>순서 역전:</b> 지연·재시도로 '주문 생성 → 취소'가 뒤바뀔: Ordering inversion: Delays and retries can flip 'order created → cancelled', so a partitioning-key strategy is essential
<b>Poison Pill:</b> 계속 실패하는 메시지가 큐를 막지 않: Poison pills: Build DLQ isolation + backoff retries + replay mechanisms so a perpetually failing message doesn't block the queue
<b>끊긴 호출 스택:</b> 비동기 이벤트는 콜스택이 끊겨, Corre: Broken call stacks: Asynchronous events sever the call stack; unless you propagate Correlation/Trace IDs in event headers and integrate with OpenTelemetry, Zipkin, or Jaeger, you can't tell "where it stopped"
<b>브로커 자체가 거대한 인프라:</b> Kafka·RabbitMQ의: The broker itself is massive infrastructure: Kafka/RabbitMQ HA, partition management, retention periods, backpressure, and consumer lag buildup
<b>이벤트 재처리:</b> 버그 수정 후 과거 이벤트를 Replay할: Event reprocessing: The complexity of replaying past events after a bug fix so that only data is resynchronized, without side effects (resending emails, etc.)
<b>신·구 버전 동시 기동:</b> 카나리/블루-그린 배포 순간 \"어: Old and new versions running simultaneously: During a canary or blue-green deployment, "which version consumes this event?" — if a schema change overlaps, an old consumer may read a new event and break, requiring a non-breaking-change strategy and a carefully ordered rollout
<b>파티션 구조 변경:</b> 트래픽 증가로 파티션을 늘리는 순간 순서: Partition structure changes: The moment you add partitions to handle traffic growth, the ordering-key mapping breaks and event order can get scrambled

이 원칙들이 교과서 속 이야기가 아니라는 것을 보여주는 사례가 <a hr: The case that shows these principles aren't just textbook theory is the cloud-native transformation of the Gov24 portal. In this project, for which uEngine Solutions performed the design and analysis, the existing Gov24 was a classic tightly coupled monolith, and in particular it carried a single point of failure (SPOF): every civil-service application had to pass through the 'Service Guide' module. If that one module stopped, every online civil service in Korea stopped with it.
전환 설계의 핵심은 앞서 본 원칙 그대로였습니다. 민원이라는 도메인을 <: The core of the transformation design was exactly the principles we've seen. The civil-service domain was divided into three types according to the nature of the business behavior, and a different pattern was applied to each.
<b style=\"font-weight: bold;\">⚡ 단순신청·즉: ⚡ Simple applications and instant issuance: Since response time is everything, synchronous REST calls were kept, but the tight coupling of directly updating other services' databases was replaced with clear API interfaces — not turning everything into events is a design decision too.
<b style=\"font-weight: bold;\">📨 유기한·비연: 📨 Deadline-based, non-integrated services: Immediate acknowledgment of receipt, then background processing via event-store-based Pub/Sub. The Saga pattern secures process consistency, while idempotency, retries, and DLQs secure reliable message handling — the exact point where the remedy for trap ③ is applied.
<b style=\"font-weight: bold;\">🏛️ 주요 민원: 🏛️ Major services (building registers, vehicle registration, etc.): Services with heavy traffic and high public impact were isolated and deployed in independent namespaces with dedicated guide channels, structurally eliminating the SPOF problem.
목표 수치는 시스템 용량 최대 <b>7.6배 자동 확장</b>, 서비스: The target figures: automatic scaling of system capacity up to 7.6x, an 81.6% reduction in service downtime, and 36.7% faster processing. It's a case that shows what outcome targets a design can take on once it has confronted "why is this hard" head-on. 사람과 AI의 유기적 협업: Seamless collaboration between people and AI
단순 반복 업무는 AI 에이전트에게, 의사결정은 사람에게. Human-i: Routine, repetitive work goes to AI agents; decisions stay with people. A human-in-the-loop (HITL) design puts a person in the seat to review and approve at every critical decision point.
AI 도입의 실제 성공 비율은 5% 미만(McKinsey)입니다. 실패한:
Fewer than 5% of AI initiatives actually succeed (McKinsey). What the failed 95% share is that they stopped at "deployment" — bolting an AI that never gets past personal-assistant duty onto the existing order of work. That never changes an organization's core processes.
The successful 5% chose "reshaping": rebuilding the work process itself from the ground up on the assumption that AI is there. Process GPT delivers that redesign as a strategy of process-centric hyperautomation — people become supervisors, or agent bosses, while AI agents run the entire process autonomously.
It is also the execution layer that Process GPT owns within the union of "judgment" and "execution" described in our vision of the AI-Native Enterprise.
초자동화를 구현한 AI-Native 기업의 압도적 성과 — 인당 매출: The standout results of AI-Native companies that achieved hyperautomation — revenue per employee
소수 정예 인력으로 압도적 인당 매출을 내는 AI-Native 기업들의: What AI-Native companies that generate extraordinary revenue per employee with small, elite teams all have in common is hyperautomation. (Source: Lean AI Native Company Leaderboard)
Process GPT — AI-Native Enterprise를 완성하는: Process GPT — the "execution" axis that completes the AI-Native Enterprise
<a href=\"blog/enterprisebrain.html\" st: The AI-Native Enterprise only comes together once an organization redesigns both "judgment" and "execution" from scratch on the assumption that AI is there. If Ontologic Platform elevates scattered databases, documents, and business rules into an ontology to create the asset that judges what affects what, then Process GPT is the execution engine that turns that judgment into who does it, when, and how on the front lines of real work. With judgment assets but no redesigned execution, insight never leaves the report; with execution but no judgment, you only get repetitive work handled faster. The skills and DMN rules Process GPT accumulates while running processes flow back into the ontology to deepen those judgment assets, and richer judgment assets in turn lead to more refined process design — a virtuous cycle, and the core axis Process GPT holds in the AI-Native Enterprise vision.
일반 사용자가 프로그래밍 개념 없이도 프로세스 흐름의 적합성만 피드백하면: Everyday users with no grasp of programming concepts simply give feedback on whether the process flow fits, and AI defines the BPMN-based process behind the scenes.
사용자 피드백이 에이전트의 스킬(Skill)과 비즈니스 규칙(DMN)으로: User feedback accumulates automatically as agent skills and business rules (DMN). Every change is version-controlled, so you can roll back to any previous state at any time.
PDF·이미지 등 비정형 규정 문서를 업로드하면 암묵지에 숨어 있던 프로: Upload unstructured policy documents such as PDFs and images, and the processes buried in tacit knowledge are identified automatically and converted into executable BPMN processes.
프로세스에 필요한 에이전트를 자동으로 식별하여 BPMN의 SwimLane: The agents a process needs are identified automatically, mapped to BPMN swimlanes (business roles), and given generated prompts.
BPMN·DMN 국제 표준 준수: Compliant with the BPMN and DMN international standards
약 20년 동안 축적된 표준 프로세스 표기법(BPMN)과 의사결정 표기법: Some 20 years of accumulated standards for process notation (BPMN) and decision notation (DMN) deliver automation that stays transparent and under your control.
